newsitem.title: USA: CFTC urges CBOT to keep Toledo as delivery point.
newsitem.headline: CFTC urges CBOT to keep Toledo as delivery point.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, in a letter dated May 5, urged the Chicago Board of Trade to reconsider its controversial proposal to drop the port of Toledo as a delivery point for soybeans and corn contracts.

Responding to comments from some 300 farm groups, grain elevators and politicians, the agency urged the exchange to "consider submitting interim or substitute changes" to the delivery terms of the contracts.
CBOT's Board of Directors responded this week, voting against the CFTC proposal at a special meeting held Wednesday.

"The exchange remains committed to our proposal because it is the best alternative overall for U.S. agriculture and the U.S. economy," CBOT's Arbor said in a release Thursday. "We will not bow to the pressures of narrow self-interests."
The CFTC had set a deadline of May 12 for the CBOT to respond to its suggested changes.

"Specifically, such changes would combine the CBOT's current proposed rule providing for the Chicago/Northern Illinois River delivery area with the addition of the current Toledo delivery point at par," the letter said.

"Implementing such changes maintaining Toledo at par with the proposed Northern Illinois River delivery area might provide a transition to a possible eventual river-only shipping certificate contract while maintaining a demonstrably viable delivery point," the letter added.

The CFTC last December ordered the exchange to propose changes within 75 days for the delivery terms of the two huge contracts because of the sharp decline in Chicago warehouse capacity for soybeans and corn.

Members of the CBOT this spring voted in favor of changes that would eliminate Toledo as a delivery point, igniting opposition from Ohio's congressional delegation and scores of eastern Corn Belt farm groups.
After being deluged with letters opposing the CBOT's proposed changes, the agency extended until June 16 the comment period before taking official action on the delivery changes.

Earlier this week, the CFTC sternly told the exchange that it had illegally listed certain soybean and corn contracts for trading in 1999 without agency approval. The contracts were the first to include the new delivery terms proposed by CBOT that eliminated Toledo warehouses.

Rep. Marcy Kaptur (D-Ohio) inserted a provision in a pending House disaster relief bill that would order the General Accounting Office to study the proposal's impact on Toledo before permitting any contract changes.
A spokesman for the CFTC said on Thursday the agency had no comment on the exchange's vote against the interim plan.
"This is a proposal still out for public comment. We'll go through the usual process and analyze the comments when the period ends June 16," the spokesman said.
